title: Bayesian Multiplicity Adjustments
text: multibayes provides tools Bayesian multiplicity adjustments. currently offers prior-odds adjustment Probability Direction (pd) via pd.adjust(), two family-wise summaries via joint(): cumulative joint statement (default) simultaneous credible intervals (interval = TRUE). Direction-agnostic directional tests supported, can mixed freely within single call.

title: Bayesian Multiplicity Adjustments
Bayesian Multiplicity Adjustments
text: Probability Direction (pd) often used decision rule: hypothesis accepted pd exceeds threshold. primary input per-test prior π0\pi_0, probability individual effect null. exchangeability expected proportion null effects family. Equivalently, may specify global null, p0 (Pr⁡(H0)\Pr(H_0)), prior probability mm hypotheses null, per-test prior recovered independence: Pr⁡(H0)=π0m,π0=Pr⁡(H0)1/m.\Pr(H_0) = \pi_0^{m}, \qquad \pi_0 = \Pr(H_0)^{1/m}. pd reweighted Bayes’ theorem: pdadj=pd⋅π1pd⋅π1+(1−pd)⋅π0pd_{\text{adj}} = \frac{pd \cdot \pi_1}{pd \cdot \pi_1 + (1 - pd) \cdot \pi_0} prior conservative (π0>π1\pi_0 > \pi_1), adjustment always shrinks pd toward lower bound. function supports two testing modes, can mixed across hypotheses within call: Direction-agnostic (direction = "two.sided"): pd = max⁡(Pr⁡(θ̂>θnull),Pr⁡(θ̂<θnull))\max\big(\Pr(\hat\theta > \theta_\text{null}),\, \Pr(\hat\theta < \theta_\text{null})\big), bounded [0.5,1][0.5, 1] construction; pdadjpd_\text{adj} also floored 0.50.5. Directional (direction = "greater" "less"): pd raw one-sided posterior probability predicted side, [0,1][0, 1]. Values 0.50.5 indicate posterior concentrated opposite predicted direction; adjustment shrink values, reflecting combined weight data conservative prior hypothesis.

title: Bayesian Multiplicity Adjustments
code: library(multibayes)  # From a vector of pd values (direction-agnostic) pd_values <- c(H1 = 0.999, H2 = 0.946, H3 = 0.813, H4 = 0.763, H5 = 0.891, H6 = 0.987)  # Specify the per-test null prior pi0 directly (primary interface) pd.adjust(pd = pd_values, pi0 = 0.65)  # ...or specify the global null p = Pr(all null); pi0 is then p^(1/m) pd.adjust(pd = pd_values, p0 = 0.4)  # Simulate posterior draws Sigma <- matrix(0, nrow = 6, ncol = 6); diag(Sigma) <- 1 mu <- c(1, -0.1, 0.8, 0, 2, 3) draws <- MASS::mvrnorm(n = 4000, mu = mu, Sigma = Sigma) colnames(draws) <- c("H1", "H2", "H3", "H4", "H5", "H6")  # From posterior draws (per-test correction only) pd.adjust(draws = draws, p0 = 0.4, null.value = 0)  # Mix of directional and agnostic tests with parameter-specific nulls pd.adjust(   draws = draws,   pi0 = 0.4,   null.value = c(0.2, 0, 0.2, 0, 0.5, 0.5),   direction  = c("greater", "two.sided", "greater", "two.sided", "greater", "greater") )

title: Bayesian Multiplicity Adjustments
text: Rejecting pd.adj > c identical rejecting raw pd > c*, c*=cπ0(1−π0)(1−c)+cπ0.c^* = \frac{c\,\pi_0}{(1-\pi_0)(1-c) + c\,\pi_0}. print header reports : e.g. pi0 = 0.7 default c = 0.975, Note. cutoff c*c^* exact transformation rule, per-test rate (0.022) uses α=2(1−c)\alpha = 2(1-c), holds diffuse prior large nn. informative prior true per-test rate smaller, reported rate conservative. Family-wise mode. Set fwer = TRUE additionally report family-wise conservative cutoff raw pd controls (prior-averaged π0\pi_0) FWER m tests. Standard corrections assume every test null (π0=1\pi_0 = 1); using π0\pi_0 relaxes 1/π01/\pi_0. prior-averaged (Bayesian) FWER, strong frequentist control.
code: Decision: raw pd > 0.9891 (adjusted from 0.975);  effective per-test alpha 0.0217 (from 0.05) pd.adjust(pd = pd_values, pi0 = 0.7, alpha = 0.05)   # same as threshold = 0.975 pd.adjust(pd = pd_values, pi0 = 0.7, fwer = TRUE) #> Decision:    raw pd > 0.9891 (adjusted from 0.975); effective per-test alpha 0.0217 (from 0.05) #> Family-wise: raw pd > 0.9959 (FWER 0.05 over m = ... under the assumed pi0; per-test alpha 0.0081)

Columns: pd (values used adjustment), pd.adj (adjusted values), pi0 (per-test null prior \(\pi_0\)), m (number tests). order = TRUE rows sorted decreasing pd. direction-agnostic tests, pd pd.adj bounded \([0.5, 1]\); directional tests, \([0, 1]\), values \(0.5\) indicating data (adjustment) favoured opposite direction. draws supplied, output additionally includes median.est (posterior median per parameter), null.value, direction. print method summarises constant quantities (pi0, m) header displays per-test table; columns remain available programmatic access. object also carries, attributes, decision cutoff threshold (\(c\)), equivalent adjusted cutoff raw pd threshold.adj (\(c^*\)), corresponding two-sided per-test Type rates alpha.nominal (\(2(1-c)\)) alpha.eff (\(2(1-c^*)\)); retrieve , e.g., attr(x, "threshold.adj"). cutoffs threshold.adj threshold.fwer exact transformations decision rule, reported per-test rates (alpha.eff, fwer calibration) use identity \(\alpha = 2(1 - c)\), holds diffuse within-model prior large \(n\) (null pd approximately uniform \([0.5, 1]\)). informative prior true per-test rate smaller, rates conservative threshold.fwer controls FWER stated level.

title: Prior-odds adjustment for Probability of Direction pd — pd.adjust
text: adjustment follows Bayes' theorem. Given per-hypothesis prior \(\pi_0\) complement \(\pi_1 = 1 - \pi_0\), adjusted pd : $$    pd_{adj} = \frac{pd \pi_1}{pd \pi_1 + (1-pd)\pi_0} $$ prior conservative (\(\pi_0 > \pi_1\)), adjustment always shrinks pd toward lower bound. Direction-agnostic tests ("two.sided"): pd defined \(\max\!\big(\Pr(\hat\theta > \theta_\text{null}),\, \Pr(\hat\theta < \theta_\text{null})\big)\) bounded \([0.5, 1]\) construction. \(pd_{adj}\) also floored \(0.5\), adjustment produces shrinkage toward \(0.5\). Directional tests ("greater" "less"): pd raw posterior probability mass predicted side, \(\Pr(\hat\theta > \theta_\text{null})\) \(\Pr(\hat\theta < \theta_\text{null})\), defined \([0, 1]\). Values pd \(0.5\) indicate posterior concentrated opposite predicted direction; adjustment shrink values toward \(0\), reflecting combined weight data conservative prior hypothesis. Mixed use directional direction-agnostic tests within call supported: element direction handled independently, prior-odds adjustment applied uniformly across hypotheses regardless directionality. pd.adjust returns per-test correction (marginal pd adjusted value pd.adj). Family-wise summaries across hypotheses, cumulative joint statement simultaneous credible intervals, provided separately joint.
